reflection.text:
Compound AZ841 unblinded as Aurora kinase inhibitors - agent call correct (p=0.89) with verdict Approve. What we got right was dose-persistent polyploidy signature, not a single well.

Acquisitions were discriminative: list_available_experiments showed 8 doses 0.01-30 uM, 4 wells budget. We bracketed with w_fd966f2782 at 0.3 uM (e2) and w_0827a3dcd3 at 10 uM (e3), then filled intermediates w_78842cb906 1 uM (e7) and w_ec63f270ae 3 uM (e8) to test persistence vs transition to toxicity. This paid off:
- e2: 425 cells, frac_large_nucleus z=+76.8, nuc_form_factor z=-36.6, nuc_solidity z=-25.4
- e7: 559 cells, frac_large_nucleus z=+60.3, nuc_form_factor z=-39.2, nuc_solidity z=-31.8
- e8: 279 cells, frac_large_nucleus z=+59.0, nuc_form_factor z=-38.2, nuc_solidity z=-31.2
Massive, same-direction effects across 3 independent single wells at 0.3/1/3 uM, with increased nuc_area / nuc_dna_integrated. describe_phenotype e4 and e10 (density similar vs DMSO, 6 and 8 observations) both flagged enlarged, lobed/multinucleated polyploid nuclei with preserved tubulin/actin - candidates Aurora kinase inhibitors only. That morphology is expected for Aurora inhibition, consistent with literature on Aurora-A loss and multinucleation PMID 30050055 and general Aurora inhibitor polyploidy phenotype PMID 22242557, PMID 24965505, PMID 28089889 - we searched 'Aurora kinase inhibitor polyploidy multinucleation phenotype' (e16: 2 hits) and 'AZ841 Aurora kinase inhibitor' (e17: 4463 hits) but had no curated AZ841 mechanism (e15: PubChem CID 12001839, ChEMBL none, from BBBC021 structure) so had to rely on phenotype alone.

compare_to_reference_atlas captured convergence: e6 over 2 wells NSC 1/2 Aurora, k-neighbours 6/10 Aurora, 4/10 Microtubule destabilizers; after adding e7/e8, e9 NSC 3/4 Aurora, 9/10 neighbours Aurora (mean 0.897) vs 1/10 Microtubule destabilizer (0.806). No DNA-damage neighbours, which correctly down-weighted hypotheses DNA damage 0.05 and Microtubule destabilizers 0.03 / Eg5 0.02 (e13). Phenotype descriptions arguing against microtubule destabilization and Eg5 (frac_mitotic_like ~0) supported that.

What misled / what we missed:
1. High-dose well e3/e5 misleads toward DNA damage / cytoskeletal effect: w_0827a3dcd3 (10 uM, 234 cells vs 425-559 at lower doses) showed nuc_form_factor z=-23.3, nuc_dna_integrated +16.5, act_glcm_contrast +14.9, microscopist e5 density lower vs DMSO with candidates Aurora, DNA damage, DNA replication, and dose_response e11 frac_large_nucleus Spearman rho=-1.00 p=0 over 4 wells. Taken literally this contradicts dose-dependence. In context it is high-dose cell loss/toxicity reducing scorable large nuclei, not true dose-response reversal - supported by opposite signal e12 nuc_form_factor rho=+0.40 p=0.6 (form factor stays low) and retained atlas similarity 0.945-0.973 in e9 despite including the 10 uM well.
2. Initial e6 4/10 Microtubule destabilizer neighbours was noise from overlapping large-nucleus morphology; resolved by adding intermediates.
3. Statistical and design gaps: each dose was rep 1 only, no true replicates, so p=0 is not credible and we cannot assess well-to-well variability per dose. Leaving p=0.89 rather than 1.0 was correctly calibrated for the discordant 10 uM well and lack of replicates, as noted in review.

We did not invent validation; next experiment remains phospho-Histone H3 Ser10 / Aurora B localization + DNA content flow cytometry vs reference Aurora inhibitor control, as proposed.
